label: Real run on this Mac's Docker Compose stack, with synthetic traffic from klaxon.traffic: synthetic data, a simulated provider, no real money. One fault from klaxon.faults, duplicate-delivery, was injected on purpose. The alert was raised by klaxon.alerts from what the stack showed. Klaxon's loop ran live on it, through Claude Code on Aravind's seat, offered one write action (rollback_deploy), which runs only if a person approves it at the gate, and stopped on diagnosed after 4 steps; any reply it got is a recorded response, not a simulation. The diagnosis was compared with the fault's recorded cause by a rule (klaxon.grading), not by a person or a model. Klaxon asked at the approval gate to act on its diagnosis; the request was approved with make approve (the request's id typed at a terminal), and the action ran: redeploy ledger-consumer: LEDGER_HANDLER naive -> idempotent, LEDGER_BAD_EVENTS dead_letter (unchanged). Code, not the model, then verified it (klaxon.agent.verify): passed; the cause is removed, and the money is not right. The fault's cause was removed by Klaxon: its rollback (Klaxon, approved request r-33b5) removed the cause, and the harness's clearing then found the good settings running, and changed nothing.

fault.name: duplicate-delivery
fault.title: Payments counted twice in the books
fault.cause: a deploy of the ledger consumer without its dedupe (LEDGER_HANDLER=naive): every webhook the provider sends again, after an acknowledgement it never got, is booked a second time
expected_symptoms: the money check fails: events counted twice, the books ahead of the provider by their amounts
the webhook dashboard stays green, and consumer lag stays at 0
the ledger stops reporting 'already processed' while the confirmer still sees the same duplicates
fault.remedy: roll the ledger consumer back to the idempotent handler, then repair each double posting with a reversal (a write, so it needs approval)

diagnosis.hypothesis: ledger-consumer was redeployed at 04:24:17Z, 17 seconds before the alert, with LEDGER_HANDLER=naive. This handler books every Kafka message it receives and never checks whether that event_id was already posted. The provider resends webhooks until they are acknowledged, so the same event can reach provider-events more than once. Each copy then becomes a new ledger transaction. evt_000308 was booked three times from three offsets (100, 101 and 103). Six other events, five charges and one refund, were booked twice. The result is $461.00 of extra provider_clearing balance. The ledger still balances because each duplicate is a full double entry. Our payments and refunds still match the provider, which places the fault in ledger posting only. The duplicate refund also explains why pay_000217 nets to 1 cent in our ledger against $24.56 at the provider.

evidence.shows: Confirms the alert. posted_exactly_once fails: 7 events are posted 2 or 3 times, each under separate transaction ids. matches_provider fails: the ledger is +$461.00 ahead of the provider. The ledger is balanced, and payments and refunds match the provider. This isolates the fault to ledger posting.
ledger-consumer is the only service changed recently. It was deployed at 04:24:17Z with LEDGER_HANDLER=naive. Every other service was created at 04:20:38Z with the stack.

ledger-consumer logged 'posted' for evt_000308 ($131.93, pay_000279) three times, at 04:24:31, 04:24:32 and 04:24:33. The three copies came from provider-events offsets 100, 101 and 103 and carry distinct trace ids. Redelivered copies of one event were each booked, with no dedup.

proposed_fix.summary: Roll ledger-consumer back to its previous settings, which should restore the idempotent handler that dedups on event_id. Then repair the ledger as a separate step. Reverse the extra transactions for the 7 events in c1 (for example 255, 266, 272, 273, 297 and the extras for evt_000298 and evt_000308), keeping one posting per event. Re-run the money check to confirm that posted_exactly_once and matches_provider pass.

diagnosis.blast_radius: The ledger-consumer container is recreated, so ledger posting pauses briefly. Kafka holds the events and the consumer group resumes from its committed offset, so nothing should be lost. payment-confirmer and payments-api are unaffected. The rollback only stops new duplicates. The $461.00 already over-booked stays wrong until the data repair is done. Left open: I did not confirm the exact previous LEDGER_HANDLER value, or whether any duplicates predate the 04:24:17 deploy. The transaction ids suggest they are all recent.
diagnosis.rollback_plan: If the rolled-back consumer misbehaves, for example by failing to post or by building up lag, redeploy ledger-consumer with its current settings. Do this only while the ledger is watched, because the current naive handler will keep double-posting. Hold off the ledger repair until the consumer is stable, and do it as reversing entries so it can itself be undone.
